data.narrative:
Transmutex is a Series A nuclear energy company founded by Franklin Servan-Schreiber, Federico Carminati, and Jean-Pierre Revol, having raised $23M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 3 public peers (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private companies in the nuclear energy sector, including Fuse Energy, X-Energy, Oklo, and Nano Nuclear Energy.

Stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable triangulation approach. Using $23M in total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to next-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $46M. Peer-median triangulation is not applicable due to insufficient comparable data points within narrow stage and tier filters; while 4 same-sector peers exist, fewer than 3 met the adjacency criteria required for reliable benchmarking.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $39M (low) to $53M (high), with a median point of $46M. This single-method triangulation reflects meaningful uncertainty around the appropriate step-up multiplier and the degree to which stage progression mechanics apply to early-stage nuclear technology ventures. Key unknowns include the company's technical progress relative to peer cohorts, capital efficiency trajectory, and whether nuclear subsector dynamics warrant adjustments to standard venture stage multipliers. Additional private comparable data or disclosed financing rounds would materially improve precision.
